overview.description: Four-player trick-taking game of the Schafkopf group (ace-ten family), played mainly in north-eastern Michigan, USA. Temporary partnerships each hand (two vs two or one vs three). Trumps are all queens, jacks, and diamonds; the diamond 7 (Spitzer) ranks second-highest. First to 42 game points wins.

history.origins: Spitzer is of the Schafkopf group of ace-ten games. It is played extensively in north-eastern Michigan (Rogers City, Alpena, Posen); regular tournaments are held. The game has clear German origins though definite evidence of play in Germany has not been found.
timeline: Play in Michigan USA; page dates from 1999, updated 2023.
history.evolution: Partnerships are determined per hand by the black queens or by calling (call for an ace, go alone, or announce Schneider).
history.cultural: Documentation maintained by John McLeod; game description based mainly on contributions from Richard Newman.

setup.players: Four players. This is a trick-taking game; players form temporary partnerships each hand (two vs two or one vs three) but keep separate scores. The object is to be the first to reach 42 or more game points.
setup.dealing: First dealer chosen by any method; deal passes left after each hand. Dealer shuffles, player to dealer's right cuts. Deal 8 cards to each player in packets: 3, then 2, then 3 to each.

rules.objective: Win tricks containing valuable cards; be the first to reach 42 or more game points. Partnerships are temporary each hand (two vs two, or one vs three if a player goes alone).
rules.gameplay: After the deal, players may call for a partner (holder of black queens), go alone (zola, stealer, or zola schneider/schwartz), or announce Schneider. Player to dealer's left leads; must follow suit; if unable, must play trump. Highest trump wins, else highest card of led suit. Winner of trick leads next. Eight tricks per hand; trick points (A=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2, 9/8/7=0) determine game points.
keyRules: 14 trumps: all queens, jacks, and diamonds; rank high to low: Club Q, Diamond 7 (Spitzer), Spade Q, Heart Q, Diamond Q, Club J, Spade J, Heart J, Diamond J, Diamond A, 10, K, 9, 8.
Non-trump (fail) in each suit rank A, 10, K, 9, 8, 7.
Must follow suit; if void, must trump.
Winning team needs more than 60 trick points; 31+ points is brush; game points from table by hand type and result.

strategy.basic: Once partner is known, direct trick points to your side; play high-value cards (A, 10, K) to partner's tricks (smearing). Lead fail aces early to win 11 points or draw trumps.
strategy.intermediate: If holding Spade Q, leading a high trump can invite partner to reveal with Club Q. Hold the Diamond 7 (Spitzer) to beat Spade Q when opportune; track which fail suits have been played.
strategy.advanced: Double-cutting a led fail ace (trumping then being overtrumped) is a key tactic. After a fail suit has been played twice, leading it again is effectively leading trump. Distribute smear cards early; later in the hand you have less control.
tips: The Diamond 7 (Spitzer) is the only card that beats the Spade Q (Little Queen) besides the Club Q.
Keep track of fail suits played; a suit cannot go around twice without being trumped.

trumpConfig.trumpSuitRanking: Club Q (high), Diamond 7 (Spitzer), Spade Q, Heart Q, Diamond Q, Club J, Spade J, Heart J, Diamond J, Diamond A, 10, K, 9, 8 (low)
trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Highest trump wins trick; if no trump, highest of led suit wins.

edgeCases.text: Called ace must be played on first trick when its suit is led by another player; holder may not discard it earlier.
If a player holds both black queens they may call for a partner, go alone (stealer), or announce a zola; if no announcement, stealer is implied.
Trick with no trick points is scored according to 0-30 or 90-120 column.

engine.handRankingSystem: Ace-ten trick point values: A=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2; 9/8/7=0. Trump order and fail order as in trumpConfig.
engine.deckDescription: A 32-card French deck formed by removing ranks 2 through 6 from a standard pack, leaving 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, and Ace in each of the four French suits.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (clubs, spades, hearts, diamonds). All queens, jacks, and diamonds count as trump; clubs, spades, and hearts are fail (non-trump) except when trump is led.
engine.rankDescription: In trump: Club Q, Diamond 7 (Spitzer), Spade Q, Heart Q, Diamond Q, Club J, Spade J, Heart J, Diamond J, Diamond A, 10, K, 9, 8. In fail: A, 10, K, 9, 8, 7.
